summary: Console alerts lose trace context after trace-attribute namespace change during retention migration
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported that console alerts that used to link to trace sessions or surface trace snippets no longer include the trace context for a subset of events after a retention migration performed on 2026-03-09. Impact: customers see alerts firing but trace links either return empty context or point to older trace entries (missing recent spans).

Impact:
- AcmeAI reports missions-critical alerting dashboards missing trace context for ~7% of alerts for their prod:us-east org.
- Affected alerts are primarily those with trace-derived dimensions (trace.user_id, trace.session_id) created in the 72h window spanning the retention compaction job.

Environment:
- Redwood prod cluster (us-east)
- Affected org: AcmeAI (dedicated capacity)
- Retention migration job run: 2026-03-09 02:00–03:40 UTC

Steps to reproduce:
1) Open AcmeAI org console -> Alerts -> locate alert rule 'high-latency-trace-errors'
2) Filter alert incidents to time window 2026-03-09 to 2026-03-11
3) Click an affected incident -> Attempt to open linked trace or view trace snippet in the incident panel

Observed behavior:
- Trace panel shows "No trace context available" or returns a trace with missing recent spans.
- Alert timeline still shows the event and token counts, but trace anchors are blank for ~7% of incidents.

Expected behavior:
- Console alert should include trace link that opens the matching trace with full span context or at least the last 2000 tokens of the trace log.

Additional notes:
- Customer began noticing this after we ran a retention compaction/migration designed to normalize attribute namespaces from older buckets.
- No increase in 5xx or ingest errors reported simultaneously.
steps_to_reproduce: Open AcmeAI org console -> Alerts -> locate alert rule 'high-latency-trace-errors'
Filter alert incidents to time window 2026-03-09 to 2026-03-11
Click an affected incident -> Attempt to open linked trace or view trace snippet in the incident panel
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): Verified customer's screenshots and timestamps; reproduced in prod for AcmeAI org by filtering to the post-migration window.
SRE finding: ingestion index contains events with migrated attribute namespace 'trace.context.*' while older events use 'trace.ctx.*'.

Query planner optimization: console-fast-path for alert->trace link resolution only consulted older index alias 'trace.ctx.*' due to cached alias map; leads to missed lookups for newly migrated events.
Retention compaction job log: job migrated 12M events for AcmeAI org; mapping change performed 2026-03-09T02:14Z and reindexed to a new partition without backfilling legacy alias metadata.
Observed that trace IDs exist in raw event store; the console lookup step is returning empty because it relies on a facet index that wasn't updated for the new namespace on read path.
Sampling note: events with high cardinality user attributes were more likely to be migrated with the new namespace; explains partial percentage impact (~7%).
comments: 2026-03-10 11:24 Maya Chen (Support): Customer filed with screenshots showing blank trace snippets and missing trace anchor links. Marking P1 due to alerting impact.
2026-03-10 12:05 Derek Patel (SRE): Confirmed reproduction in prod for org AcmeAI. Attached query plan and example trace_id: trace_0x7f9a1c. Looks like alias mismatch on the console read path.

2026-03-10 13:40 Liam O'Connor (Infra): Retention compaction job logs show attribute rename from trace.ctx.* -> trace.context.* and new partition created. We missed updating the alias map used by console lookups; rolling back alias map to include both prefixes as a temporary workaround.

2026-03-11 09:02 Derek Patel (SRE): Deployed temporary alias patch to console read layer; customer reports trace links restored for ~85% of previously affected incidents. Continuing to investigate full fix.

2026-03-12 16:10 Maya Chen (Support): Customer (AcmeAI) confirmed partial improvement but asked for a durable solution addressing historic migrated events. Requested ETA and any manual backfill options.

2026-03-13 10:22 Engineering: Preparing a console patch to accept both 'trace.ctx.*' and 'trace.context.*' namespaces and a backfill job to reindex the facet used by alert linking. PRs linked in metadata.
workarounds: Applied temporary alias map update in console read layer to consult both namespaces; reduces incidence of missing links.
Customer can re-run alert evaluation over a wider window to surface older events until backfill completes.
If urgent, we can run an org-scoped reindex job for affected time window (manual, takes ~2–4 hours for AcmeAI)
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation applied: alias map update rolled at 2026-03-11 09:00 UTC (console stable).

Planned remediation: patch console lookup to accept both namespaces and schedule a reindex/backfill for the affected partitions. Engineering PRs opened and code review in progress (see related_github_prs).
Follow-up action: Add migration-runbook step to update console alias cache immediately after retention compaction jobs to avoid future races. Confluence page updated.
Customer update: Provided ETA for durable backfill and requested notification when job completes.
next_steps: Finish code patch to console read path to accept both namespaces (owner: @engineering/tracing).
Schedule and run reindex/backfill for AcmeAI affected partitions during low-traffic window; communicate maintenance window with customer.
Add post-migration alias cache refresh to the retention migration runbook and automate in the pipeline.
Monitor alert link success rate for AcmeAI for 72h after backfill; escalate if >1% regression persists.
